title: Company-wide policies and processes (Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendor, Travel, Templates)
author: Asha Menon
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standardized processes that apply across teams and business units. It covers access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and the central internal templates repository. The goal is to provide a single reference for owners and operators so processes are consistent, auditable, and aligned with our security and compliance commitments.

Scope & Purpose:

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and consultants who interact with company systems, data, vendors, or who incur company expenses.
- Establishes minimum requirements and approved workflows. Local teams may add stricter controls but may not relax requirements in this document.

Ownership & Governance:

- Policy owner: People Ops (primary), with functional owners as noted for each section (Security, Finance, Eng Infra, Legal).
- Review cadence: Annual review by People Ops and reviewers listed above; critical changes require Security and Finance sign-off.
- Escalation: For exceptions and urgent issues, contact the People Ops on-call and cc the Security Incident Response channel.

1) Access & Permissions:

Purpose: Provide a least-privilege model and a repeatable account lifecycle to reduce risk and enable audits.

Key rules:
- Role-based access control (RBAC) is enforced for all production systems. Role definitions are stored in the RBAC catalog (see related pages).
- Default access: new employees receive baseline access via the new-hire onboarding playbook. Additional privileges require manager request plus owner approval.
- Time-bound access: elevated access (e.g., sudo, db-admin, billing) must be requested through the access request workflow and set to expire within the requested window.
- MFA required for all interactive accounts; hardware MFA recommended for privileged users.

Access request & provisioning (high level):
1. Submit request using the Access Request form (link in templates). Include justification, duration, and approver.
2. Manager approves in the HR system. Security reviews critical privileges within 48 hours.
3. Infra or the system owner provisions and records the grant in the access log.
4. Access is auto-revoked at expiration; owners receive an upcoming-expiry notification 7 days prior.

Permissions matrix (summary):
- Viewer: read-only dashboards, runbooks, docs.
- Developer: deploy to non-prod, create infra in sandbox projects.
- Service Operator: deploy to production via CI with RBAC CI role; no secret export.
- Admin: manage configs, rotate keys; requires two approvers.

Required artifacts for privileged access requests:
- Business justification, scope of access (systems & resources), duration, and approver.
- For access to customer data, attach Data Access Justification (per Data Management section).

2) Change Management:

Purpose: Ensure production changes are planned, tested, communicated, and reversible.

Definitions:
- Standard change: low-risk, pre-approved operational changes (routine deploys within normal CI process).
- Normal change: non-emergency changes that require change ticket and approvals.
- Emergency change: fixes to restore service; must be documented and followed with a post-implementation review.

Process (normal change):
1. Create a Change Request (CR) in the change system (include owner, impact, rollback plan, test plan, and scheduled window).
2. Security and SRE review (within 72 hours for non-urgent changes).
3. Change Advisory Board (CAB) review required for high-impact changes (>2 services or >5% user impact).
4. Implement during approved maintenance window.
5. Post-implementation verification and update CR with outcome.
6. All emergency changes require a postmortem that includes timeline, root cause, and follow-ups.

Change window guidance:
- Standard deploys: 09:00-18:00 local business days.
- High-risk changes: schedule in low traffic periods; SRE may require midnight window for infra changes.

Rollbacks & testing:
- Every change must include a clear rollback plan and measurable success criteria (health checks, key metrics).
- Canary and gradual rollout patterns are required for code that affects customer-facing features.

3) Data Management:

Purpose: Protect data confidentiality, integrity, and availability while enabling product and analytics work.

Data classification levels:
- Public: intended for external release.
- Internal: company business data not intended for public distribution.
- Confidential: customer PII, credentials, and regulated data.
- Restricted: highest sensitivity (encryption keys, signing keys, and security secrets).

Storage & handling rules:
- Confidential and Restricted data must be stored in approved systems with encryption at rest and in transit.
- Access to Confidential data requires an approved Data Access Justification and periodic access reviews every 90 days.
- Exporting data off-platform requires compliance review and, in the case of regulated workloads, legal approval.

Retention & deletion:
- Default retention: product telemetry and logs retained 365 days unless otherwise specified.
- Customer data retention is defined per contract; follow Contract Data Retention matrix (see related pages).
- Data deletion requests (e.g., GDPR/CCPA) must follow the Data Subject Request process and be completed within 30 days.

Data breach & incident response:
- Follow the Security Incident Response playbook for suspected data exposure.
- Notify Legal and People Ops within 4 hours for incidents impacting customer data.

4) Procurement & Expenses:

Purpose: Standardize vendor spend, approvals, and employee expense reimbursement to maintain budget controls and compliance.

Procurement workflow (summary):
1. Small purchases (<$5,000): manager approval in procurement tool.
2. Medium purchases ($5,000- $50,000): requires manager + Finance review.
3. Large purchases (>$50,000): requires Manager, Finance, and Legal approval; sourcing process and vendor evaluation required.

Purchase order & contract steps:
- All purchases for services or long-term commitments require a PO and an approved contract.
- Legal reviews any contract with data, security, or IP implications.

Expense policy highlights:
- Employees should use the company card for business travel where available.
- Reimbursements require itemized receipts and a completed expense report within 30 days of expense.
- Meal limits: domestic up to $75 per person; exceptions require pre-approval.
- Travel class: domestic coach; international flights require manager approval for premium economy or above.

Expense submission checklist:
- Itemized receipt, business purpose, attendee list (if applicable), project or cost center.
- Card transactions still require a receipt and justification.

5) Vendor Management & Third-Party Risk:

Purpose: Reduce risk from third-party relationships and ensure contractual protections, especially for vendors with access to systems or customer data.

Vendor onboarding checklist:
- Business justification and scope of services.
- Security questionnaire: completed and reviewed by Security.
- Data handling agreement if vendor processes customer or confidential data.
- Insurance and SLAs reviewed by Legal and Finance.
- List of vendor contacts and escalation path recorded in the vendor registry.

Vendor lifecycle controls:
- Quarterly vendor risk reviews for critical vendors.
- Contract renewals require updated security posture review.
- Offboarding: revoke credentials, terminate access, and confirm data return or secure deletion.

6) Travel & Expense Policy (summary):

- Purpose: Support safe and responsible business travel while maintaining controls.
- Pre-approval: All international travel requires manager pre-approval and must be entered into the Travel system.
- Booking: Use approved travel partners; exception requests go to People Ops.
- Safety: Employees traveling to high-risk locations must register and check advisories; company travel insurance applies.

Per diem & reimbursement examples:
- Domestic per diem: up to $75/day for meals.
- Lodging: book standard room; upgrades require manager approval.

7) Internal Templates & Standard Forms:

A central templates folder contains canonical forms and checklists. Key templates include:
- Access Request Form (Access_Request_Template.md)
- Change Request Template (Change_Request_Template.md)
- Data Access Justification (Data_Access_Justification.md)
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.md)
- Expense Report Template (Expense_Report_Template.xlsx)

Template usage rules:
- Teams must use canonical templates for approvals. Custom local fields are allowed but the core fields must remain unchanged.
- Templates are versioned; reference the template version in any request to enable audits.

Appendix A - Example: Expense report minimum fields:
- Date of expense
- Card used (company/personal)
- Amount (local currency)
- Merchant and receipt (attach)
- Business purpose and project code

Appendix B - Example: Access request minimum fields:
- Requested user
- Systems and roles requested
- Justification and duration
- Approver name and timestamp

Exceptions & Waivers:
- Exceptions to these policies must be requested through the Exceptions Request form and require an explicit owner and expiration date. Exceptions are logged and reviewed quarterly.

Auditing & Reporting:
- People Ops and Security will run quarterly audits for privileged access, vendor contracts, and expense exceptions.
- Findings are reported to the Executive Team and tracked until closed.
